SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p709/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p709/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p709/r3.claim: A following question asks why 36:14 says the messengers were strengthened with a third rather than saying three messengers were sent together; no answer appears here.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p709/r3.anchor: دلالة قوله تعالى في سورة يس (فعززنا بثالث) ولماذا لم يشير إلى إرسال ثلاثة رسل معاً؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وكعب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r1.claim: They take the messengers as prophets sent by God; the recipients’ claim that they are ordinary humans supports this reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r1.anchor: وهذه المحاورة لا تكون إلا مع من أرسله الله، وهذا قول ابن عباس وكعب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r2.speaker: قتادة وغيرهم من الحواريين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r2.claim: They say Jesus sent the three disciples after the crucifixion episode, as his followers dispersed; the group reached idol-worshipping Antioch.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة وغيرهم من الحواريين: بعثهم عيسى عليه السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r3.speaker: وهب وكعب الأحبار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r3.claim: They identify the first two messengers as Ṣādiq and Ṣadūq; other names are reported by al-Naqqāsh and Muqātil.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r3.anchor: صادق وصدوق، قاله وهب وكعب الأحبار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r4.speaker: مجاهد وابن قتيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r4.claim: They explain «fa-ʿazzaznā» as strengthening and supporting the first two; related idioms describe firm camel flesh and rain compacting earth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r4.anchor: فعززنا بثالث: أي قوينا وشددنا، قاله مجاهد وابن قتيبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r5.speaker: الحسن، وأبو حيوة، وأبو بكر، والمفضل، وأبان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r5.claim: They read the verb with a light zāy; Abū ʿAlī explains this as «we prevailed», comparing the expression in 38:23.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r5.anchor: وقرأ الحسن، وأبو حيوة، وأبو بكر، والمفضل، وأبان: بالتخفيف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r6.claim: He identifies the third messenger as Shamʿūn al-Ṣafā; Kaʿb and Wahb instead report Shalūm or Yūnus.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r6.anchor: والثالث شمعون الصفا، قاله ابن عباس. وقال كعب، ووهب: شلوم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r7.claim: The object of «strengthened» is omitted: the third messenger strengthened the first two, and together they prevailed with argument and tactful invitation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r7.anchor: وحذف مفعول فعززنا مشددا، أي قويناهما بثالث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r8.claim: The first claim «we are sent» begins an assertion without emphasis; the second adds emphatic lām as an answer to denial of revelation. The messengers entrust their truth to God and are responsible only for clear delivery.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r8.anchor: وجاء أولا مرسلون بغير لام لأنه ابتداء إخبار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r9.claim: The clarity of the message is shown by signs in the story, including curing the congenitally blind and lepers and reviving the dead.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53/r9.anchor: من إبراء الأكمه والأبرص وإحياء الميت

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r1.claim: The sūrah recalls a town warned by two messengers, then a third helper; its people rejected them, blamed the warning signs, threatened them, and were destroyed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r1.anchor: two messengers were sent by God to warn its people

TABRISI:36:11-20/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:11-20/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:11-20/r1.claim: At the king’s request, the messengers restore a blind boy’s sight with clay pupils; Shimon then challenges the king to ask his powerless deity to perform the same sign.
TABRISI:36:11-20/r1.anchor: حتى انشق موضع البصر فأخذا بندقتين من الطين فوضعا في حدقتيه

TABRISI:36:11-20/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:11-20/r5.speaker: العياشي
TABRISI:36:11-20/r5.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits a similar account through al-Thumālī and others from Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbd Allāh; variants place the envoys in Antioch, say Jesus sent them, and say Jesus then sent his legatee Shimon to rescue them.
TABRISI:36:11-20/r5.anchor: وقد روى مثل ذلك العياشي بإسناده عن الثمالي وغيره عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله ع إلا أن في بعض الروايات

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:11-14/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:11-14/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:11-14/r6.claim: Two of Jesus's disciples came first and were rejected, so God strengthened the message with a third messenger.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:11-14/r6.anchor: إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين } من الحواريين { فكذبوهما فعززنا بثالث } قوينا الرسالة برسول ثالث.

RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r3.claim: The town is Antioch and its three messengers were from Jesus’ followers, the nearest messengers to the people before Muhammad’s time.
RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r3.anchor: والقرية أنطاكية والمرسلون من قوم عيسى وهم أقرب مرسل أرسل إلى قوم إلى زمان محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وهم ثلاثة

RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r4.claim: One possible parsing makes “when We sent” an appositive to “when they came,” describing the parable as the sending to the town’s people.
RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r4.anchor: أن يكون إذ أرسلنا بدلا من إذ جاءها

RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r5.claim: Rāzī prefers the clearer parsing in which the time clause modifies “they came”: the messengers came when God sent them, not on their own initiative.
RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r5.anchor: وهو الأصح والأوضح أن يكون إذ ظرفا

RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r6.claim: Although the messengers were sent by Jesus, God calls their commission His own: an authorized messenger of God’s messenger is also God’s messenger, consoling Muhammad that rejection of them equals rejection of him.
RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r6.anchor: إرسال عيسى عليه السلام هو إرسالنا ورسول رسول الله بإذن الله رسول الله فلا يقع لك يا محمد أن أولئك كانوا رسل الرسول وأنت رسول الله فإن تكذيبهم كتكذيبك فتتم التسلية

RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r7.claim: This supports the legal principle that an agent appointed with the principal’s permission is the principal’s agent, removable by the principal but not by the intermediate agent.
RAZI-FULL:v26p45/r7.anchor: وهذا يؤيد مسألة فقهية وهي أن وكيل الوكيل بإذن الموكل وكيل الموكل لا وكيل الوكيل حتى لا ينعزل بعزل الوكيل إياه وينعزل إذا عزله الموكل الأول

STUDYQURAN:36:13/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r1.claim: The Prophet is told to give the Quraysh an example of the fate of people who treated earlier message bearers as they were treating him.
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r1.anchor: provide the Quraysh with an example of the fate that befell those who treated previous message bearers as they were treating him.

STUDYQURAN:36:13/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r4.speaker: Most commentators
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r4.claim: Most commentators take the message bearers, called mursalīn rather than rusul, to be apostles whom Jesus sent to the town.
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r4.anchor: Most commentators view the message bearers ( mursalīn, rather than rusul,“messengers”) as apostles sent to the town by Jesus.

STUDYQURAN:36:13/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r5.speaker: Most commentators
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r5.claim: In the apostles interpretation, God's sending them means Jesus was commanded by God to send them.
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r5.anchor: that God is said to have sent them indicates that Jesus was commanded by God to send them (Q, Ṭs).

STUDYQURAN:36:13/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r6.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r6.claim: Commentators report that the townspeople beat and imprisoned the first two message bearers.
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r6.anchor: After the first two were sent, the people of the town beat and imprisoned them (Q, Ṭ, Ṭs).

STUDYQURAN:36:13/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r7.speaker: Some
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r7.claim: Some say the king ordered the punishment of the first two, after which a third message bearer was sent.
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r7.anchor: Some say this punishment was ordered by the king (Aj), after which a third message bearer,

STUDYQURAN:36:13/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r8.speaker: Some
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r8.claim: Some identify the third message bearer as Jonas.
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r8.anchor: a third message bearer, whom some identify as Jonas, was sent.

STUDYQURAN:36:13/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r9.speaker: Another opinion
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r9.claim: Another opinion identifies the message bearers as prophets, rather than apostles sent by a prophet.
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r9.anchor: According to another opinion, the message bearers are prophets (Aj, Ṭs) rather than apostles sent by a prophet.

STUDYQURAN:36:13/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r10.claim: The author finds the prophets interpretation more likely: Muhammad is called a mursal in 36:3 and 2:252, and other prophets are called mursalūn in many verses.
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r10.anchor: This interpretation seems more likely, as the Prophet Muhammad is referred to as a mursal (message bearer) in v. 3 and in 2:252

STUDYQURAN:36:13/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r11.claim: The declaration here and in verse 16 may also be translated, “we are message bearers unto you.”
STUDYQURAN:36:13/r11.anchor: We have been sent unto you here and in v. 16 could also be rendered, “we are message bearers unto you.”

BURSEVI:v7p295/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p295/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p295/r9.claim: The second إذ is apposition to the first and describes when two were sent to the town's people.
BURSEVI:v7p295/r9.anchor: بدل من إذ الأولى أي : وقت أرسلنا اثنين إلى أصحاب القرية

BURSEVI:v7p295/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p295/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p295/r10.claim: The two messengers were Yahya and Yunus; their mission is attributed to God because it was by His command.
BURSEVI:v7p295/r10.anchor: وهما يحيى ويونس ونسبة إرسالهما إليه تعالى بناء على أنه بأمره تعالى

BURSEVI:v7p296/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p296/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p296/r1.claim: A legal analogy supports attributing the mission to God: an agent authorized to appoint a subagent at his discretion makes that subagent the principal's agent, so the original agent cannot dismiss him but the principal can.
BURSEVI:v7p296/r1.anchor: ويؤيده مسألة فقهية وهي أن وكيل الوكيل بإذن الموكل بأن قال الموكل له اعمل برأيك يكون وكيلا للموكل لا للوكيل

BURSEVI:v7p296/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p296/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v7p296/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the messengers came, called the people to the truth, and were promptly denied, beaten, and imprisoned.
BURSEVI:v7p296/r2.anchor: وضربوهما وحبسوهما على ما قال ابن عباس

BURSEVI:v7p296/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p296/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p296/r3.claim: Fa-ʿazzaznā means “we strengthened them”; the object is omitted because the preceding context supplies it, while the focus is on the one who strengthened them and His subtle plan for truth to prevail.
BURSEVI:v7p296/r3.anchor: قويناهما فحذف المفعول لدلالة ما قبله عليه ولأن القصد ذكر المعزز به

BURSEVI:v7p296/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p296/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p296/r4.claim: The root can describe rain compacting earth, hard ground, or meat becoming firm; Taj al-Masadir glosses taʿzīz as strengthening, and a hadith phrase is glossed as making someone firm.
BURSEVI:v7p296/r4.anchor: يقال عزز المطر الأرض إذا لبدها وسددها

BURSEVI:v7p296/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p296/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p296/r5.claim: The third was Shimon al-Saffar, also called Shimon al-Sakhra, leader of the Apostles and Jesus's successor after his ascension.
BURSEVI:v7p296/r5.anchor: هو شمعون الصفار ويقال له شمعون الصخرة أيضا رئيس الحواريين وقد كان خليفة عيسى عليه السلام بعد رفعه إلى السماء

BURSEVI:v7p296/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p296/r6.speaker: التكملة
BURSEVI:v7p296/r6.claim: Al-Takmila reports disagreement over whether the three were prophets sent by God or Apostles sent by Jesus; on the latter view, God's mission is attributed to Jesus because he sent them under God's command.
BURSEVI:v7p296/r6.anchor: قال في "التكملة" : اختلف في المرسلين الثلاثة فقيل : كانوا أنبياء رسلا أرسلهم الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v7p296/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p296/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p296/r7.claim: From the Apostles interpretation the author infers the Apostles were not prophets during Jesus's life or after his ascension.
BURSEVI:v7p296/r7.anchor: علم منه أن الحواريين لم يكونوا أنبياء لا في زمان عيسى ولا بعد رفعه

BURSEVI:v7p296/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p296/r8.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p296/r8.claim: The author cites the Prophet's statement “There is no prophet between me and him,” taking him to mean Jesus; he allows that it may mean a prophet bringing an independent law, which would not rule out a prophet confirming an earlier law.
BURSEVI:v7p296/r8.anchor: بقوله عليه السلام : "ليس بيني وبينه نبي" أي : بين عيسى وإن احتمل

BURSEVI:v7p296/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p296/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p296/r9.claim: All the messengers speak together, emphasizing their claim because rejection has already occurred; rejecting the first two amounts to rejecting the third because their message is unified.
BURSEVI:v7p296/r9.anchor: أي : جميعا {إنا إليكم مرسلون} مؤكدين كلامهم

BURSEVI:v7p296/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p296/r10.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v7p296/r10.claim: Kashf al-Asrar says God told Jesus to send his Apostles to cities before his ascension; two went to Antioch, and an angel could give them luminous wine that enabled them to understand the local language.
BURSEVI:v7p296/r10.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : (قصه آنست كه رب العالمين وحى فرستاد بعيسى عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v7p296/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p296/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p296/r11.claim: The people to whom the messengers were sent worshipped idols.

BURSEVI:v7p297/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p297/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه وكعب الأحبار
BURSEVI:v7p297/r1.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih and Kaʿb al-Ahbar say the king also disbelieved and joined his people in persisting in torturing and killing the messengers.
BURSEVI:v7p297/r1.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه وكعب الأحبار : بل كفر الملك أيضا وأصروا جميعا هو وقومه

BURSEVI:v7p297/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p297/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p297/r2.claim: The author supports the report that the king disbelieved: had he or some of his people believed, they would have aided the messengers as the carpenter martyr did, especially since people follow their kings and the proof was clear.
BURSEVI:v7p297/r2.anchor: ويؤيده حكاية تماديهم في اللجاج والعناد وركوبهم متن المكابرة في الحجاج

TAB-FULL:v19p413/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p413/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p413/r2.claim: Qatada reports that Jesus sent two of his disciples to Antioch; its people rejected them, so Jesus strengthened them with a third.
TAB-FULL:v19p413/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {واضرب لهم مثلا أصحاب القرية إذ جاءها المرسلون إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين فكذبوهما فعززنا بثالث} [يس: 14] قال:

TAB-FULL:v19p413/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p413/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وكعب الأحبار ووهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v19p413/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas, Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, and Wahb ibn Munabbih says God sent three envoys—Ṣādiq, Maṣdūq, and Salūm—to a pagan king of Antioch; two came first, then God reinforced them with a third, and the king threatened them.
TAB-FULL:v19p413/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، وعن كعب الأحبار، وعن وهب بن منبه، قال: " كان بمدينة أنطاكية فرعون من الفراعنة

TAB-FULL:v19p415/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p415/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p415/r1.claim: God sent two messengers to call the people to Him; when they rejected them, He strengthened the pair with a third.
TAB-FULL:v19p415/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {فعززنا بثالث} [يس: 14] قال: شددنا

TAB-FULL:v19p415/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p415/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v19p415/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses the verb as “we strengthened them.”
TAB-FULL:v19p415/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {فعززنا بثالث} [يس: 14] قال: شددنا

TAB-FULL:v19p415/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p415/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v19p415/r3.claim: Mujahid also glosses the phrase as “we increased [their number].”
TAB-FULL:v19p415/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله {فعززنا بثالث} [يس: 14] قال: «زدنا»

TAB-FULL:v19p415/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p415/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v19p415/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says God made them three; this is reinforcement, and reinforcement means strength.

TAB-FULL:v19p415#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p415#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p415#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the three messengers announced that they were sent to call the people to worship God alone and renounce their idols, a mission they were strengthened to deliver.
TAB-FULL:v19p415#2/r1.anchor: والقراءة عندنا بالتشديد لإجماع الحجة من القراء عليه

TAB-FULL:v19p415#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p415#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p415#2/r2.claim: All readers except ʿĀṣim read the verb with a doubled zāy, “strengthened”; ʿĀṣim lightens it, “overcame.” Al-Ṭabarī prefers the doubled reading by the readers’ consensus because “overcame” fits poorly here.
TAB-FULL:v19p415#2/r2.anchor: والقراءة عندنا بالتشديد لإجماع الحجة من القراء عليه

TABATABAI:36:13-15/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:13-15/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:13-15/r5.claim: تعزيز derives from عزّة and means strengthening and fortification.
TABATABAI:36:13-15/r5.anchor: التعزيز من العزة بمعنى القوة والمنعة

TABATABAI:36:13-15/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:13-15/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:13-15/r6.claim: The sending of the two messengers elaborates the earlier mention of messengers coming to the town: the people rejected them, God strengthened them with a third, and the messengers declared their commission from God.
TABATABAI:36:13-15/r6.anchor: بيان تفصيلي لقوله { إذ جاءها المرسلون }

TABATABAI:36:13-32/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:13-32/r2.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:36:13-32/r2.claim: Al-Majmaʿ relates that Jesus sent two disciples to Antioch; after they healed Habib al-Najjar's ill son, the king interrogated and beat them, and news of their miracles spread.
TABATABAI:36:13-32/r2.anchor: في المجمع قالوا بعث عيسى رسولين من الحواريين إلى مدينة أنطاكية فلما قربا من المدينة رأيا شيخا

TABATABAI:36:13-32/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:13-32/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TABATABAI:36:13-32/r3.claim: Wahb says the messengers never reached the king; he imprisoned and flogged them, so Jesus sent Shimʿun al-Ṣafa undercover. Shimʿun befriended the court, arranged a public test, and the messengers restored sight to a blind youth and raised a seven-day dead man, prompting some to believe.
TABATABAI:36:13-32/r3.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه بعث عيسى هذين الرسولين إلى أنطاكية فأتياها ولم يصلا إلى ملكها

TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r1.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī, through al-Thumālī and others, reports a variant in which God sent two messengers and then a third, Jesus sent Shimʿun to rescue them, and the revived dead man was the king's son; the king and his people believed.
TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r1.anchor: عن الثمالي وغيره عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام إلا أن في بعض الروايات

TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r2.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says the king disbelieved and joined his people in resolving to kill the messengers; Habib, at the city's far gate, ran to urge obedience to them.
TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق بل كفر الملك وأجمع هو وقومه على قتل الرسل

TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r3.claim: The author says the Qur'anic narrative's sequence does not fit some of the transmitted versions.
TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r3.anchor: أقول سياق آيات القصة لا يلائم بعض هذه الروايات

TABRISI:36:14/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14/r1.speaker: أبو بكر
TABRISI:36:14/r1.claim: Abu Bakr reads fa-ʿazaznā with a light z; the other readers use the doubled z form.
TABRISI:36:14/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو بكر { فعززنا } بالتخفيف والباقون بتشديد الزاي

TABRISI:36:14/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14/r6.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:36:14/r6.claim: Abu Ali says the doubled form means to strengthen and increase, while the light form means to overpower, as in the cited verse.
TABRISI:36:14/r6.anchor: قال أبو علي: قال بعضهم عززنا قوينا وكثرنا وأما عززنا فغلبنا

TABRISI:36:14-19/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14-19/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:36:14-19/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the townspeople beat and imprisoned the first two messengers.

TABRISI:36:14-19/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14-19/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:14-19/r6.claim: The strengthened form means God reinforced and supported the two with a third messenger; it derives from might and protection, as in the proverb about the victor taking spoils.
TABRISI:36:14-19/r6.anchor: أي فقويناهما وشددنا ظهورهما برسول ثالث مأخوذ من العزة وهي القوة والمنعة

TABRISI:36:14-19/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14-19/r7.speaker: شعبة
TABRISI:36:14-19/r7.claim: Shu'ba gives the first messengers' names as Shimon and John, and the third's as Paul.
TABRISI:36:14-19/r7.anchor: قال شعبة: كان اسم الرسولين شمعون ويوحنا

TABRISI:36:14-19/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14-19/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وكعب
TABRISI:36:14-19/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ka'b name the messengers Sadiq and Saduq, with Salum as the third.
TABRISI:36:14-19/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وكعب: صادق وصدوق والثالث سلوم

TABRISI:36:14-19/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14-19/r9.speaker: وهب وكعب
TABRISI:36:14-19/r9.claim: Another view identifies them as Jesus' apostles; God attributes them to Himself because Jesus sent them by His command.
TABRISI:36:14-19/r9.anchor: عن وهب وكعب قالا: وإنما أضافهم تعالى إلى نفسه

TABRISI:36:14-19/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14-19/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:14-19/r10.claim: The messengers tell the people of the town that God has sent them to them.
TABRISI:36:14-19/r10.anchor: أي قالوا لهم يا أهل القرية إن الله أرسلنا إليكم

THALABI:v8p125/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p125/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v8p125/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas names the two envoys Tarus and Marus.
THALABI:v8p125/r1.anchor: واختلفوا في اسميهما، فقال ابن عباس: تاروص وماروص،

THALABI:v8p125/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p125/r2.speaker: وهب
THALABI:v8p125/r2.claim: Wahb names them Yahya and Yunus.
THALABI:v8p125/r2.anchor: وقال وهب: يحيى ويونس، ومقاتل: تومان ومانوص

THALABI:v8p125/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p125/r3.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v8p125/r3.claim: Muqatil names them Tuman and Manus.
THALABI:v8p125/r3.anchor: وقال وهب: يحيى ويونس، ومقاتل: تومان ومانوص

THALABI:v8p125/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p125/r4.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف وعاصم عن حفص
THALABI:v8p125/r4.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif and Asim through Hafs read فعززنا with a lightened consonant, glossed as overcoming opponents through a third envoy.
THALABI:v8p125/r4.anchor: قرأ طلحة بن مصرف وعاصم عن حفص: فعززنا مخففا، أي فغلبناهم

THALABI:v8p125/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p125/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p125/r5.anchor: من عزيز برسول ثالث وهو شمعون

THALABI:v8p125/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p125/r6.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v8p125/r6.claim: Muqatil calls the third envoy Shaman.
THALABI:v8p125/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: شمعان، وقال كعب: الرسولان صادق وصدوق

THALABI:v8p125/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p125/r7.speaker: كعب
THALABI:v8p125/r7.claim: Ka'b names the first two envoys Sadiq and Saduq and the third Shalum.
THALABI:v8p125/r7.anchor: وقال كعب: الرسولان صادق وصدوق والثالث شلوم

THALABI:v8p125/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p125/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p125/r8.claim: God is credited with sending them because Jesus sent them by God's command, and they belonged among God's messengers.
THALABI:v8p125/r8.anchor: وإنما أضاف الإرسال إليه لأن عيسى (عليه السلام) إنما بعثهم بأمره عز وجل، وكانوا في جملة الرسل،

THALABI:v8p125/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p125/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p125/r9.claim: All three envoys tell the people of Antioch they were sent to them.
THALABI:v8p125/r9.anchor: فقالوا جميعا لأهل أنطاكية: إنا إليكم مرسلون.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r1.claim: إذ أرسلنا is an apposition to إذ جاءها: they came through God's sending two messengers; the sending is attributed to God because Jesus sent them by God's command.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r1.anchor: {إذ أرسلنا} بدل من قوله: {إذ جاءها} والمعنى: إذ جاؤها (¬6) بإرسالنا إليهم اثنين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi dates the event to the time when Jesus was raised to heaven.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: وكان ذلك حين رفع إلى السماء (¬1).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people beat and imprisoned the two messengers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq and all the commentators explain the third messenger as strengthening and reinforcing the mission.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r4.anchor: {فعززنا بثالث} قال أبو إسحاق: (فقوينا وشددنا الرسالة برسول ثالث) (¬3). وهو قول جميع المفسرين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r5.speaker: المبرد وأبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad and Abu Ali say the doubled reading means strengthened, while the light reading means overcame or prevailed; Abu Ali cites the related wording in 38:23 and a Jarir line for the latter sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r5.anchor: قال المبرد وأبو علي: من قرأ فعززنا بالتشديد، فالمعنى: شددنا وقوينا. ومن قرأ بالتخفيف، فمعناه: قهرنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r6.claim: Abu Ubayd says their recitation is doubled, explaining it as overcoming or prevailing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r6.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: وقراءتنا بالتشديد. لأن تأويل عززنا: غلبنا (¬9).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r7.claim: Al-Wahidi says the first explanation, strengthening the mission with a third messenger, better fits the meaning.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r8.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r8.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj say both pronunciations can carry the sense of strengthening, like saying شددنا with light or doubled consonants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r8.anchor: [وقال الفراء: عززنا] (¬10). وعززنا كقولك: شددنا وشددنا بالتخفيف والتثقيل (¬11). ونحو ذلك قال الزجاج.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r9.claim: The ones who say they were sent are the messengers addressing the people of Antioch.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p463#2/r9.anchor: {فقالوا}: يعني الرسل لأهل أنطاكية. {إنا إليكم مرسلون}.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r4.speaker: ابن مجاهد عن أبيه
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r4.claim: Ibn Mujāhid's father glosses the phrase as strengthening the two with a third.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r4.anchor: تفسير ابن مجاهد، عن أبيه: فشددنا بثالث

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r5.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says God strengthened the two with a third; two prophets had been sent and killed, so God sent a third to them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r5.anchor: وتفسير السدي: يعني: فشددنا، يعني: فقويناهما بثالث، أنه أرسل إليهما نبيان فقتلوهما

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r6.claim: The first two messengers spoke before the third arrived, and the third spoke after them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803/r6.anchor: قال: فقالوا، يعني: الأولين قبل الثالث والثالث بعدهما

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r1.claim: The townspeople deny that the messengers are sent by God, answering that they are merely humans like them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r1.anchor: {إنا إليكم مرسلون {14} قالوا ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا} [يس: 14-15] وجحدوا أنهم رسل

QASHANI:36:13-14/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:36:13-14/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:36:13-14/r2.claim: The body rejects spirit and heart for lack of affinity and because they differ from it in light and darkness.

QASHANI:36:13-14/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:36:13-14/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:36:13-14/r3.claim: The third messenger is intellect, which accords with the self in interests and successes and influences it and its people by calling them to what heart and spirit call for.
QASHANI:36:13-14/r3.anchor: فعززوا بالعقل الذي يوافق النفس في المصالح والمناجح ويدعوها وقومها إلى ما يدعو إليه القلب والروح فيؤثر فيهم

QASHANI:36:13-14/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:36:13-14/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:36:13-14/r4.claim: Their bad omen is aversion to the messengers' call to discipline and spiritual struggle, which denies them pleasures and benefits.
QASHANI:36:13-14/r4.anchor: تنفرهم عنهم لحملهم إياهم على الرياضة والمجاهدة ومنعهم عن اللذات والحظوظ

QASHANI:36:13-14/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:36:13-14/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:36:13-14/r5.claim: Stoning the messengers means pelting them with natural impulses and bodily demands; tormenting them means dominating and using them to obtain animal and predatory appetites.
QASHANI:36:13-14/r5.anchor: رميهم بالدواعي الطبيعية والمطالب البدنية. وتعذيبهم إياهم: استيلاؤهم عليهم واستعمالهم في تحصيل الشهوات والبهيمية والسبعية

ELMALILI:36:13-27/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r3.claim: The town is reported to be Antioch and its messengers to have been sent from among Jesus' disciples.
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r3.anchor: Burada bu karye Antakya, mürselûn da Îsâ aleyhisselâm’ın Havâriyyûnundan gönderilenler olduğu naklediliyor

ELMALILI:36:13-27/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r5.claim: The plain sense indicates that the messengers were envoys granted prophethood by God.
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r5.anchor: bunların taraf-ı ilâhîden nübüvvet verilmiş resuller olduklarını

ELMALILI:36:13-27/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r8.speaker: Katâde ve gayrıları
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r8.claim: Qatada and others say these were apostles from Jesus' disciples, sent when Jesus was raised up.
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r8.anchor: Katâde ve gayrıları demişlerdir ki bunlar

ELMALILI:36:13-27/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r9.claim: Even if Jesus sent the disciples, the verse says 'We sent' because Jesus' mission was itself by God's command.
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r9.anchor: Hazret-i Îsâ tarafından gönderilmeleri de Allah teâlâ’nın emriyle olduğundan dolayı olmuş oluyor

ELMALILI:36:13-27/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r10.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r10.claim: Some identify the first two as John and Paul and the third as Simon Peter.
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r10.anchor: Bazıları bu ikisinın Yuhanna ile Pavlus olduğunu

ELMALILI:36:13-27/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r11.claim: Since representation is the passage's chief aim, the strengthening of two by a third signals the honor of Muhammad's apostleship: Muhammad's message confirms and strengthens the missions of Moses and Jesus.
ELMALILI:36:13-27/r11.anchor: Yani ikinin bir üçüncü ile takviyesi Mûsâ ve Îsâ aleyhimesselâm’ın ahîren risâlet-i Muhammediye ile

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r1.claim: The town's persistent rejection of three prophets, scorn for a believer who supported them, and likely murder of him is set before the Meccan opponents of Muhammad as a cautionary example.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r1.anchor: Kendilerine üç peygamber birden gönderilmesine rağmen inkârcılıkta direnen

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r4.claim: After the people rejected the first two messengers, a third was sent to reinforce them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r4.anchor: Halkın iki elçiyi dinlememesi üzerine bir üçüncüsü gönderilmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r7.claim: Neither the Qur'an nor sound hadith identifies the town, its inhabitants, or the messengers sent there.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r7.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de ve sahih hadislerde burada sözü edilen şehrin neresi, ahalisinin ve gönderilen elçilerin kimler olduğuna dair bilgi bulunmamaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r8.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r8.claim: Exegetical accounts identify the town as Antioch, the messengers as Jesus' apostles, and the inhabitants as Romans.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r8.anchor: Tefsirlerde söz konusu yerleşim merkezinin Antakya ve gönderilen elçilerin ise Hz. Îsâ’nın havârileri olduğu belirtilir; buna göre karye halkı da Romalılar olmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r9.claim: The Antioch-apostles identification is unsound because verse 14 says the messengers were sent by God, not by Jesus.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r9.anchor: 14. âyette elçilerin Allah tarafından gönderildiği ifade edildiğine göre bunların Hz. Îsâ tarafından yollanan havâriler şeklinde anlaşılması isabetli olmaz.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r10.claim: The New Testament places Barnabas, Peter, and Paul in Antioch after Jesus' ascension, so Jesus did not send them there.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r10.anchor: Kaldı ki Yeni Ahid’de Antakya’ya gittiği belirtilen Barnabas, Petrus ve Paul’ün oraya gidişleri Îsâ’nın semaya urûcundan sonra olmuştur yani bunlar onun tarafından da gönderilmiş değildirler.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r11.claim: The apostles met no resistance in Antioch, its people soon believed in Jesus, and the city later became a major Christian center.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r11.anchor: Öte yandan havâriler Antakya’da herhangi bir direnişle karşılaşmamış, bu yerin halkı Hz. Îsâ’ya inanmakta gecikmemiş ve şehir bir müddet sonra Hıristiyanlığın belli başlı merkezlerinden biri olmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r12.speaker: İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r12.claim: Exegetes' accounts of the messengers' names, whether God or Jesus sent them, and how they were treated conflict; Ibn Atiyya omitted the material because it was unreliable.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r12.anchor: İbn Atıyye de zikredilen bu bilgiler sağlıklı olmadığı için kendisinin ihtisar yolunu tuttuğunu belirtir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r21.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r21.claim: The story warns those who persist in rejecting God's message and opposing His messengers, warns Muhammad's deniers, and strengthens his followers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r21.anchor: bir taraftan Hz. Muhammed’in peygamberliğini inkâr edenlere güçlü bir uyarı yaparken diğer yandan da ona tâbi olanların mâneviyatını yükseltmektir.

ITQAN:v4p391/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p391/r15.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p391/r15.claim: The two messengers sent to the people are identified as Simon and John, with Paul as the third.

ITQAN:v4p391/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p391/r16.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v4p391/r16.claim: An alternative names the messengers Sadiq, Saduq, and Shalum.

ITQAN:v3p173#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p173#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p173#3/r1.claim: Emphasis may use inna, anna, lām, ala, amma, ha, ka-anna, lakin, layta, laʿalla, pronouns, qad, future markers, emphatic nuns and negative particles.
ITQAN:v3p173#3/r1.anchor: وهي إن وأن ولام الابتداء والقسم وألا الاستفتاحية وأما وها التنبيه وكأن

ITQAN:v3p173#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p173#3/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p173#3/r2.claim: Emphasis is apt when the addressee doubts or denies; its strength varies with the intensity of denial.
ITQAN:v3p173#3/r2.anchor: وإنما يحسن تأكيد الكلام بها إذا كان المخاطب به منكرا أو مترددا

ITQAN:v3p173#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p173#3/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p173#3/r3.claim: In the first denial, Jesus’s messengers use inna and a nominal sentence; after stronger denial they add an oath and lām as well.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p186/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p186/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p186/r1.claim: The Yā Sīn narrative, including the messengers’ arrival and the people’s threat, follows an implied question-and-answer pattern; al-Jurjānī says this reading applies throughout the passage.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p186/r1.anchor: التقدير الذي قدرناه من معنى السؤال والجواب بين في ذلك كله

DAMGHANI:v1p322/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r12.claim: Fa-ʿazzaznā means that God strengthened the two messengers by sending a third.

FARRA:v2p373#2/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p373#2/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p373#2/r2.claim: The third messenger had been sent before the first two and rejected; the narrative mentions him later, so “we reinforced with a third” refers back to him.
FARRA:v2p373#2/r2.anchor: بالثالث الذي قبلهما كقولك: فعززنا بال

FARRA:v2p373#2/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p373#2/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p373#2/r3.claim: The strengthening came through what the first messenger, Shimon, had taught the pair.
FARRA:v2p373#2/r3.anchor: التعزيز يقول: شددنا أمرهما بما علمهما الأول شمعون

FARRA:v2p373#2/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p373#2/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p373#2/r4.claim: The messengers had been sent to Antioch.

FARRA:v2p373#2/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p373#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v2p373#2/r5.claim: Abd Allah reads “with the third”; the definite noun follows because the messenger had already been mentioned among the messengers, like asking where the two dirhams are after mentioning them.
FARRA:v2p373#2/r5.anchor: وهي في قراءة عبد الله (فعززنا بالثالث) لأنه قد ذكر فى المرسلين

FARRA:v2p373#2/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p373#2/r6.speaker: عاصم
FARRA:v2p373#2/r6.claim: ʿĀṣim reads ʿazzaznā lightly; al-Farrāʾ says it has the same sense as shaddadnā, “we strengthened.”
FARRA:v2p373#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ عاصم (فعززنا) خفيفة. وهو كقولك: شددنا وشددنا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p364#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p364#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p364#2/r1.claim: ʿAzzaznā means We strengthened and reinforced; ʿazaza minhu means strengthen someone's heart, and camel meat teʿazzaza when it hardens.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p364#2/r1.anchor: {فعززنا بثالث} أي قوينا وشددنا. يقال: عزز منه؛ أي قو من قلبه. وتعزز لحم الناقة: إذ صلب.

MAJAZ:v2p158/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p158/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p158/r3.claim: ʿAzaznā means We strengthened and reinforced them; al-Namir ibn Tawlab’s line with ʿazat is cited as evidence.
MAJAZ:v2p158/r3.anchor: «فعززنا بثالث» (14) أي قوينا وشددنا قال النمر بن تولب:

MAJAZ:v2p158/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p158/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p158/r4.claim: He explains the proverb man ʿazza bazza as the victor seizing what he wants, and bazza itself as taking away; ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib’s verse witnesses the usage.
MAJAZ:v2p158/r4.anchor: يقال فى المثل من عز بز : من قهر سلب وتفسير «بز» انتزع،

NAHHAS:v3p387/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p387/r4.speaker: عاصم
NAHHAS:v3p387/r4.claim: Asim reads فعززنا; al-Nahhas rejects deriving it from عز يعز and instead connects it with عازني, meaning I overcame him.
NAHHAS:v3p387/r4.anchor: وقرأ عاصم ( فعززنا ) وربما غلط في هذا بعض الناس

NAHHAS:v3p387/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p387/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p387/r5.claim: The verb derives from عازني فلان فعززته: I overcame and subdued him; the form has Arabic parallels.
NAHHAS:v3p387/r5.anchor: إنما هو من قول العرب عازني فلان فعززته أعزه أي غلبته وقهرته

NAHHAS:v3p387/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p387/r6.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p387/r6.claim: Al-Farra says the third, Simon, was sent before the first two; فعززنا به means he overcame them.
NAHHAS:v3p387/r6.anchor: وتأول الفراء فعززنا بثالث أن الثالث أرسل قبل الاثنين وأنه شمعون وإن معنى فعززنا به أنه غلبهم

NAHHAS:v3p387/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p387/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p387/r7.claim: The apparent wording opposes al-Farra; an earlier messenger would more naturally be introduced as بالثالث.
NAHHAS:v3p387/r7.anchor: والظاهر يدل على خلاف ما قال ولو كان كما قال لكان الأولى في كلام العرب أن يقال بالثالث

SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r1.speaker: أبو بكر
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r1.claim: Abu Bakr reads with light ز, meaning We overcame; cf. 38:23.
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r1.anchor: أبو بكر بتخفيف الزاي بمعنى غلبنا

SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r2.claim: من عز بز means whoever prevailed took the property.
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r2.anchor: ومنه قولهم: " من عز بز " أي صار له بز.

SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r3.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r3.claim: The other reading doubles ز and means We strengthened.

SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r4.claim: Both readings omit the object: strengthen or overcome the two messengers with a third.
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r4.anchor: وعلى كلتا القراءتين المفعول محذوف أي: فقويناهما بثالث أو فغلبناهما بثالث.

SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r5.speaker: عبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r5.claim: Abd Allah reads بالثالث with the article.
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r5.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله " بالثالث " بألف ولام.

SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r6.claim: Plain denial receives إن; emphatic later denial receives إن and lām.
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r6.anchor: لأنهم في الأولى استعملوا مجرد الإنكار فقابلتهم الرسل بتوكيد واحد

SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r7.claim: Arabic assertions are initial, requestive, and emphatic denial.
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r7.anchor: قال أهل البيان: الأخبار ثلاثة أقسام: ابتدائي وطلبي وإنكاري

SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r8.speaker: أبو العباس الكندي
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r8.claim: Al-Kindi says the three forms have different meanings, not redundancy.
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r8.anchor: جاء إلى أبي العباس الكندي فقال: إني أجد في كلام العرب حشوا

SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r9.claim: Al-Samin identifies al-Kindi as the man asked to imitate Quran who opened to al-Maida and desisted.
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r9.anchor: هذا هو الكندي الذي سئل أن يعارض القرآن ففتح المصحف فرأى سورة المائدة فكع عن ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r10.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r10.claim: Al-Shaykh says the first is initial information and the second answers denial with lām.
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r10.anchor: وجاء أولا " مرسلون " بغير لام؛ لأنه ابتداء إخبار

SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r11.claim: Al-Samin says al-Shaykh confuses requestive with initial context.
SAMIN-DURR:36:14/r11.anchor: وهذا قصور عن فهم ما قاله أهل البيان

ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r2.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r2.claim: Tafsir identifies the town as Antioch and says Jesus sent two messengers there, whom its people rejected.
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r2.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنهم أهل إنطاكية، وجه إليهم عيسى اثنين فكذبوهما

ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r3.claim: The verb is read with either gemination or a light consonant.
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r3.anchor: ويقرأ فعززنا - بالتشديد والتخفيف - ومعنى فعززنا

ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r4.claim: The phrase means that God strengthened and reinforced the message with a third messenger.
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r4.anchor: ومعنى فعززنا فقوينا وشددنا الرسالة بثالث أي برسول ثالث

ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r5.claim: The messengers told the people that their duty was only to deliver the message.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p710/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p710/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p710/r1.claim: God first sent two messengers; after the people rejected them, He supported them with a third rather than sending all three at once.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p710/r1.anchor: أرسل رسولين أول مرة فكذبهما القوم فقوّاهما تعالى برسول ثالث

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p710/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p710/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p710/r2.claim: The wording “we strengthened” means the mission and call were strengthened, rather than the two messengers personally.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p710/r2.anchor: التعزيز ليس للرسل أنفسهم وإنما التعزيز يكون للدعوة التي يدعو الرسل لها

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r4.claim: The city account warns Quraysh that rejecting God's messengers leads to destruction: the first two are rejected, a third supports them, and the people dismiss signs, blame bad luck, and threaten the messengers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r4.anchor: The Almighty sent two of His messengers to warn the inhabitants of this city; however, they denied both of them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r5.speaker: exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r5.claim: Exegetes identify the unnamed city as Antioch and its messengers as envoys selected from Jesus's disciples, rather than messengers sent by God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r5.anchor: Our exegetes are of the opinion that the reference is to Antioch and the messengers mentioned here are not the messengers of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r1.claim: The messengers' manner of introduction and their claim under oath show that they are God's envoys, not emissaries of Jesus; their audience's objection to their humanity fits a claim to divine prophethood.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r1.anchor: they are not envoys of Jesus (sws); rather they are envoys of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r2.claim: A destruction of Antioch during Jesus's time would appear in the Gospels and Bible histories, but those sources omit it and historical accounts instead say Antioch led in accepting Jesus.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r2.anchor: neither the Gospels nor Bible history mention it. In fact, history bears witness to the contrary;

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r5.claim: Jesus's mission was to Israel, not the surrounding nations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r5.anchor: Jesus (sws) was a messenger sent to the Israelites.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r6.claim: Jesus stopped his disciples from carrying his message to other nations, undercutting the Antioch identification.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r6.anchor: He in fact stopped his disciples from going to other nations.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r7.claim: Islahi calls the Antioch view baseless and introduces several reasons against it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p378/r7.anchor: In my opinion, this view is baseless because of a number of reasons.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p381/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p381/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p381/r4.claim: Verse 14 explains the sending mentioned in verse 13: two messengers came first, were rejected, and then received God's help through a third, after which they called people to obey their message.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p381/r4.anchor: The Almighty initially sent two messengers to them but they rejected these messengers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p381/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p381/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p381/r5.claim: The two are Moses and Aaron; Islahi says this is the sole instance in prophetic history of two messengers being sent simultaneously to one people, an arrangement discussed in earlier sūrahs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p381/r5.anchor: there is only once instance when two messengers were simultaneously sent by God to a people.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p382/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p382/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p382/r1.claim: Islahi says the Qur’an introduces the third helper at verse 20 and records his memorable speech in support of Moses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p382/r1.anchor: The Qur’ān has introduced him in verse 20 ahead

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p382/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p382/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p382/r2.claim: Though no messenger in the technical sense, the believer courageously defended the messengers; Islahi compares his standing among Moses's followers to Abū Bakr's among Muhammad's.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p382/r2.anchor: Though he was not a messenger in the technical sense, yet he undertook a fearless effort to defend and support the messengers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p382/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p382/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p382/r4.claim: The believer belonged to Pharaoh's royal family, advocated truth, and sympathized with Moses even before Moses received prophethood.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p382/r4.anchor: It is evident from verse 40 of Sūrah Mu’min that he belonged to the royal family and was a great advocate of the truth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p382/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p382/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p382/r5.claim: After Pharaoh and his courtiers decided to kill Moses, the believer spoke in Pharaoh's court; Islahi cites that speech from verses 26–45 of Sūrah Mu’min as evidence of his status and support.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p382/r5.anchor: This speech is cited by the Qur’ān in Sūrah Mu’min.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r1.speaker: Pharaoh
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r1.claim: Pharaoh proposes killing Moses, claiming fear that Moses will change their religion and spread disorder, and daring him to call on his Lord for aid.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r1.anchor: The Pharaoh said to his courtiers: “Let me slay Moses; if he is truthful let him call his Lord.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r2.speaker: Moses
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r2.claim: Moses seeks God's protection from every arrogant person who rejects the Day of Reckoning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r2.anchor: Moses said: “I take refuge with my Lord and your Lord from the evil of every arrogant person

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r3.speaker: a believer from the Pharaoh’s family
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r3.claim: The hidden believer objects to killing a man who worships God and brings clear signs: if Moses is false, harm is his; if true, some threatened punishment will reach them, and God does not vindicate a blatant liar or transgressor.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r3.anchor: But a believer from the Pharaoh’s family who had till then hidden his faith, said: “Would you slay a man merely because he says:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r4.speaker: a believer from the Pharaoh’s family
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r4.claim: The believer warns that present dominance cannot save them from God's torment and that God does not approve of servants being oppressed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r4.anchor: a believer from the Pharaoh’s family who had till then hidden his faith, said:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r5.speaker: Pharaoh
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r5.claim: Pharaoh counters that his considered opinion is sound and that he is guiding the people on the straight path.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r5.anchor: The Pharaoh said: “I am giving my calculated opinion and remember that I am guiding you towards exactly the straight path.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r6.speaker: a believer from the Pharaoh’s family
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r6.claim: The believer warns of the punishments that overtook Noah's people, ʿĀd, Thamūd, and later nations; he fears the coming Day of flight with no rescuer, recalls Egypt's doubts after Joseph's clear signs, and warns that one whom God misguides has no guide.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r6.anchor: And he who had embraced faith said: “O People of My Nation! I fear the same punishment will befall you

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r7.claim: Islahi explains that those who overstep bounds and dispute revelations without proof are hated by God and believers, and that God seals every arrogant tyrant's heart.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r7.anchor: In this manner does God lead astray those who exceed bounds and are afflicted with doubts

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r8.speaker: Pharaoh
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r8.claim: Pharaoh orders Hāmān to build a tower from which he can inspect the heavens for Moses's Lord, whom he declares a liar.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p383/r8.anchor: Pharaoh said: “O Hāmān! Build me a tower that I may peep in the edges of the heavens

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p384/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p384/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p384/r1.claim: The believer addressed Egypt's royal court when Pharaoh proposed killing Moses; after hiding his faith until this decisive moment, he openly revealed it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p384/r1.anchor: This speech was delivered by the true believer to the House of Lords of Egypt before all the courtiers and nobles.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p384/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p384/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p384/r2.claim: His royal-family status meant the courtiers could not dismiss his advice as bias in favor of the Israelites.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p384/r2.anchor: he was a noble of the royal family; hence his advice could not have been regarded to be one given in bias for the Israelites.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p384/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p384/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p384/r3.claim: God's mention of helping with a third celebrates this nobleman's courageous public support for Moses and the messengers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p384/r3.anchor: It is this shinning feat and ever-famous exploit of this great person that is mentioned by Almighty

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p384/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p384/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p384/r4.claim: The arguments and fearless manner of his defense of Moses have no parallel except among God's prophets and the righteous.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p384/r4.anchor: the fearless nature in which he spoke has no parallel except in the history of prophets of God and the righteous.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p385/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p385/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p385/r1.claim: The plural claim to be sent does not make all three equal in rank; it is a collective expression in which the dominant member is implied, like members of one embassy speaking together.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p385/r1.anchor: This linguistic style is one in which the dominant element is implied.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p385/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p385/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p385/r2.claim: Moses alone was the primary messenger; Aaron assisted him, while the third man was a courageous supporter who undertook to preach Moses' message and was grouped with the messengers for that work.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p385/r2.anchor: only Moses (sws) was the real messenger. Aaron (sws) too was not the primary messenger

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p38#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p38#2/r1.speaker: عاصم في رواية أبي بكر والمفضل
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p38#2/r1.claim: Abu Bakr's and al-Mufaddal's transmissions from Asim read فعززنا with a light ز; the others, including Hafs, double it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p38#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ عاصم في رواية أبي بكر والمفضل [عن عاصم]: فعززنا خفيفة. وقرأ الباقون، وحفص عن عاصم: فعززنا مشددة الزاي.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p38#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p38#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p38#2/r2.claim: One explanation gives the light form the sense strengthened and increased, while the doubled form means overcame, as in 38:23.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p38#2/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم: عززنا: قوينا وكثرنا. وأما عززنا: فغلبنا من قوله: وعزني في الخطاب [ص/ 23]

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p38#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p38#2/r3.speaker: جرير
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p38#2/r3.claim: Jarir's line using أعزك is cited as poetic evidence for the sense overcame.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p38#2/r3.anchor: وقال جرير: أعزك بالحجاز وإن تسهل بغور الأرض تنتهب انتهابا

NASHR:v2p353/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p353/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
NASHR:v2p353/r2.claim: Abū Bakr reads fa-ʿazaznā with a light zāy; all other readers double it.
NASHR:v2p353/r2.anchor: فروى أبو بكر بتخفيف الزاي وقرأ الباقون بتشديدها

QIRAAT-ER:36:14:8#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:36:14:8#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:36:14:8#1/r1.claim: The single-zāy Form I variant may mean became mighty or overcame, and transitively We overpowered or made rare; it shifts from intensive reinforcement to simple strengthening.
QIRAAT-ER:36:14:8#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant with single zāy (Form I: 'azaza instead of Form II: 'azzaza)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p140#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p140#5/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p140#5/r1.claim: Qatāda reports that Jesus sent two of his disciples to the people of Antioch, then sent a third after them.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p140#5/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين ﴾ قال بلغني أن عيسى ابن مريم بعث

ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r1.claim: The sending of two is placed in the story to complete its parable and console the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r1.anchor: بناء على أنه كان أمره تعالى لتكميل التمثيل وتتميم التسلية

ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r2.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ka'b say the two were messengers sent by God; a distinguished scholar chose this view and said they supported Jesus and confirmed his law, like Aaron supported Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r2.anchor: إبن عباس وكعب هم رسل الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r3.claim: The divine-messenger view is supported by the wording that God sent them and by the people's objection that they were human, assuming divine messengers must not be human.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r3.anchor: وأيد بظاهر ( إذ أرسلنا إليهم إثنين )

ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r4.claim: Some cite reports of miracles such as healing the blind and reviving the dead, since miracles properly belong to prophets.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r4.anchor: وأستدل البعض على ذلك بظهور المعجزة كإبراء الأكمه وأحياء الميت

ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r5.claim: Opponents answer that the apostles may have spoken as direct envoys or been treated as representatives; reported miracles could be Jesus's confirming wonder through them, not proof they claimed direct divine mission.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r5.anchor: ومن ذهب إلى الأول أجاب عن الأول بما سمعت وعن الثاني بأنهم إما أن يكونوا دعوهم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r6.claim: Reports name the two as Yuhanna and Bulus; Tuman and Bulus according to Muqatil; Shimon and Yuhanna by Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i; Sadiq and Saduq by Wahb and Ka'b; or Nazoos and Maroos.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل تومان وبولس وقال شعيب الجبائي شمعون ويوحنا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r7.claim: The text says they were sent to the people rather than to the town, because sending properly takes people as destination and this prepares for their rejection.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r7.anchor: ليطابق إذ جاءها لأن الإرسال حقيقة إنما يكون إليهم لا إليها

ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r8.claim: Rejection attaches more clearly to people as object; the explanatory fa resembles Moses striking the stone, after which water gushed forth.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r8.anchor: نظير التعقيب في قوله تعالى : ( فقلنا أضرب بعصاك الحجر فأنفجرت )

ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r9.claim: The village inhabitants were idol worshippers; azzazna means God strengthened and reinforced the two.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r9.anchor: فعززنا ( أي قويناهما وشددنا قاله مجاهد وإبن قتيبة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r10.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r10.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Qutayba gloss the verb as strengthening; other lexicographers give related senses of flesh hardening and rain compacting earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r10.anchor: قاله مجاهد وإبن قتيبة وقال يقال تعزز لحم الناقة إذا صلب

ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r11.claim: The verb omits its object, understood as the two messengers from the preceding clause; the third as means of reinforcement is the point.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p220#3/r11.anchor: لدلالة ما قبله عليه ولأن المقصود ذكر المعزز به

ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r1.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the third was Shimon al-Safa, also called Samaan; Wahb and Ka'b call him Shalum; Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i gives Bulus, spelled with sad by him and sin by some.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r1.anchor: على ما روى عن إبن عباس شمعون الصفا ويقال سمعان أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r2.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r2.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu Haywa, Abu Bakr, al-Mufaddal, and Aban read without doubling the zay; the light and doubled forms are synonymous.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو حيوة وأبو بكر والمفضل وأبان ( فعززنا ) بالتخفيف

ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r3.speaker: أبو علي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r3.claim: Abu Ali derives the light form from azzahu, to overcome, invoking the proverb that whoever overcomes takes spoils; the third's proof defeated the opponents.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r3.anchor: وقال أبو علي المخفف من عزه إذا غلبه ومنه قولهم من عزيز أي من غلب سلب

ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r4.speaker: عبدالله
ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r4.claim: Abdullah reads with the phrase bil-thalith, with the third.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r5.claim: The fa coordinates their statement after denial and reinforcement; plural attribution works if all agreed, even if one spoke while the rest concurred.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p221/r5.anchor: عطف على فكذبوهما فعززنا والفاء للتعقيب أي فقال الثلاثة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.claim: Ordinals from two through ten use the fāʿil pattern in an annexation to the counted noun; Sībawayh cites ثاني اثنين and ثالث ثلاثة.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.anchor: فبناء الاثنين وما بعده إلى العشرة فاعل وهو مضاف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.claim: Feminine ordinals use the feminine ending on fāʿila and ثنتين/اثنتين, while three through ten omit the feminine hāʾ.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.anchor: وتترك الهاء في ثلاث وما فوقها إلى العشر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.claim: خامس أربعة means the one who makes four into five; this formation is rare in actual speech though regular by analogy, and Arabs do not say ثاني واحد.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.claim: From eleven to nineteen, forms such as حادي عشر and ثالث عشر have both parts open and behave as a single name, like خمسة عشر.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.claim: The feminine ordinal system distinguishes forms such as حادية عشرة, marking the ordinal as feminine and treating عشرة as in خمس عشرة.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.anchor: وتترك الهاء في ثلاث وما فوقها إلى العشر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.claim: When saying خامس خمسة, speakers can say خامس خمسة عشر and حادي أحد عشر; if حادي أحد عشر is used, حادي declines because أحد عشر is already indeclinable, unless all three words are fused.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.anchor: فإن بنيت حادي وما أشبهه معها صارت ثلاثة أشياء اسما واحدا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.speaker: بعضهم
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.claim: Some say ثالث عشر ثلاثة عشر and similar forms by analogy, but omit the final counted number for ease because the remaining words signal it; this is less common than ثالث عشر.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.anchor: ثالث عشر ثلاثة عشر ونحوه وهو القياس

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.claim: Masculine ordinals dominate in mixed-gender counts: حادي أحد عشر for ten women and a man, and خامس خمسة for four women and a man.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.anchor: وتقول هذا حادي أحد عشر إذا كن عشر نسوة معهن رجل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.claim: خامس أربع means that he makes four women into five; Arabs scarcely use this form.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.anchor: ولا تكاد العرب تكلم به كما ذكرت لك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.claim: The same ordinal pattern extends to higher counts, such as رابع ثلاثة عشر; بضعة عشر and بضعة عشرة inflect like تسعة عشر and تسع عشرة respectively.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابذكركالاسمالذيبهتبينالعدة.anchor: وأما بضعة عشر فبمنزلة تسعة عشر في كل شيء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r1.speaker: وهب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r1.claim: Wahb names the first two messengers John and Paul.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r2.claim: The verb means that God strengthened the two messengers with a third.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r4.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r4.claim: Abu Bakr's transmission from Asim reads the verb without doubling the z; it has the same sense as the doubled form, like lightened and doubled forms of “strengthened.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم: "فعززنا" بالتخفيف وهو بمعنى الأول كقولك: شددنا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r5.claim: Another explanation takes the verb to mean “we overcame,” from the saying “whoever prevails takes it.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r5.anchor: وقيل: أي: فغلبنا من قولهم: من عز بز.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r6.speaker: كعب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r6.claim: Kaʿb names the first two messengers Sadiq and Sadduq and the third Shalum; God attributes their dispatch to Himself because Jesus sent them by God's command.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r6.anchor: وقال كعب: الرسولان: صادق وصدوق، والثالث شلوم، وإنما أضاف الله الإرسال إليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p12#3/r7.claim: All three messengers address the people of Antioch and declare that they were sent to them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r1.claim: The two envoys were Yaḥyā and Yūnus, according to one identification.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r2.claim: Another view says the two envoys were people other than Yaḥyā and Yūnus.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r4.speaker: أبو بكر
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r4.claim: Abū Bakr reads the verb without doubling, from ʿazzahu meaning “he overcame him”; its object is omitted because the preceding context supplies it and the helper is the focus.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر مخففا من عزه إذا غلبه

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r5.anchor: ذكر المعزز به. { بثالث } وهو شمعون

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r6.claim: The people worshipped idols; Jesus sent two envoys, who met Ḥabīb al-Najjār tending sheep. They healed his sick son, and many others were healed, so the news reached the king.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r6.anchor: وذلك أنهم كانوا عبدة أصنام فأرسل إليهم عيسى عليه السلام اثنين

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r7.claim: When the king asked whether another god existed, the envoys named the creator of the king and his idols. The king imprisoned them, and Jesus sent Simon, who entered in disguise and befriended the court and king.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r7.anchor: ثم بعث عيسى شمعون فدخل متنكرا وعاشر أصحاب الملك

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r8.claim: Simon arranged for the envoys to answer the king, who asked for signs; they prayed for a blind boy and his sight was restored, then challenged the idols to do the same.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r8.anchor: الله الذي خلق كل شيء وليس له شريك

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r9.claim: The king admitted that the idols neither hear nor see nor harm nor benefit. He then demanded resurrection; the envoys prayed, and a boy dead for seven days rose and warned the people of the seven valleys of Fire.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r9.anchor: آلهتنا لا تسمع ولا تبصر ولا تضر ولا تنفع

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r10.claim: The revived boy said he saw a handsome young man in heaven interceding for the three envoys; the king recognized Simon and the two others.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r10.anchor: فرأيت شابا حسنا يشفع لهؤلاء الثلاثة

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r11.claim: Simon saw that his words had affected the king and urged him; the king and a group believed, while Gabriel cried out against the unbelievers and they perished.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:14/r11.anchor: ومن لم يؤمن صاح عليهم جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام فهلكوا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r1.claim: God sent two messengers so each could support the other and strengthen their mission; they announced that they had been sent to call the people to faith in God.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r1.anchor: ليعضد أحدهما الآخر فيكون أشد لأمرهما فأخبراهم بإرسالها إليهم كأن قالا : نحن رسولان إليكم لتؤمنوا بالله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r2.claim: The townspeople denied the messengers despite their signs; God sends no messenger without signs of the kind by which people may believe, directly or through another messenger.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r2.anchor: لأنه من المعلوم أنا ما أرسلنا رسولا إلا كان معه من الآيات ما مثله آمن عليه البشر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r3.speaker: طفيل بن عمرو الدوسي
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r3.claim: As an example of a sign requested from the Prophet, Tufayl ibn Amr al-Dawsi received a light on his forehead and, after asking, on his whip instead.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r3.anchor: كما كان للطفيل بن عمرو الدوسي ذي النور لما ذهب إلى قومه وسأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن تكون آية

BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r4.claim: ʿAzzaznā means that God brought might, strength, and victory to His cause or His messenger after the messengers were weakened by denial.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r4.anchor: فأوقعنا العزة , وهي القوة والشدة والغلبة , لأمرنا أو لرسولنا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r5.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r5.claim: Abu Bakr's transmission from ʿAsim reads ʿazaznā with a lightened consonant, supporting the sense of bringing victory or might.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r5.anchor: بما أشارت إليه قراءة أبي بكر عن عاصم بالتخفيف

BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p250/r6.claim: God sent a third messenger with the same commission as the first two, and the three reiterated that they had been sent specifically to this people.

DURR-FULL:v7p50/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r1.claim: The account identifies the third envoy as Simon, one of the disciples, and says the interval without a messenger lasted 434 years.
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r1.anchor: وهو قوله {إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين فكذبوهما فعززنا بثالث} والذي عززبه: شمعون وكان من الحواريين وكانت الفترة التي ليس فيها رسول أربعمائة سنة وأربعة وثلاثين سنة

DURR-FULL:v7p50/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r2.claim: Qatada says Jesus sent two disciples to the people of Antioch and followed them with a third.
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r2.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين} قال: بلغني أن عيسى بن مريم بعث إلى أهل القرية - وهي انطاكية - رجلين من الحواريين واتبعهم بثالث

DURR-FULL:v7p50/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the third envoy strengthened the proof against the people; the envoys called them to worship God alone, but they rejected them.
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية رضي الله عنه في قوله {إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين فكذبوهما فعززنا بثالث} قال: لكي تكون عليهم الحجة أشد فأتوا أهل القرية فدعوهم إلى الله وحده

DURR-FULL:v7p50/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r4.speaker: شعيب الجبائي
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r4.claim: Shuʿayb al-Jubbaʾi names the first two envoys Simon and Yuhanna and the third Paul.
