DURR-FULL:v7p50/r4.anchor: عن شعيب الجبائي قال: اسم الرسولين اللذين قالا {إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين} شمعون ويوحنا واسم (الثالث) بولص

DURR-FULL:v7p50/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r5.claim: Mujahid reports a lighter reading of fa-ʿazzaznā.
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {فعززنا بثالث} مخففة

DURR-FULL:v7p50/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r6.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr identifies the helper as Simon son of Yuhanna and also names Paul as the third; he says all three were killed, then Habib, who had concealed his faith, urged the people to follow them and was killed in a well at al-Rass.
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه في قوله {إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين} قال: اسم الثالث الذي عزز به سمعون بن يوحنا والثالث بولص فزعموا أن الثلاثة قتلوا جميعا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3191#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3191#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3191#3/r1.claim: Qatādah says he had heard that Jesus son of Mary sent two of the disciples to Antioch and followed them with a third.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3191#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله ، عنه في قوله : اذ ارسلنا اليهم اثنين قال : بلغني ان عيسى بن مريم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3191#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3191#3/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3191#3/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says the third messenger made the proof stronger; the messengers called the townspeople to worship God alone, without a partner, but they rejected them.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3191#3/r2.anchor: عن أبي العالية رضي الله ، عنه في قوله : اذ ارسلنا اليهم اثنين فكذبوهما فعززنا بثالث قال : لكي تكون عليهم الحجة اشد

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3191#3/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3191#3/r3.speaker: شعيب الجبائي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3191#3/r3.claim: Shuʿayb al-Jubbāʾī names the two messengers Shimʿūn and Yūḥannā, and the third messenger Būluṣ.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3191#3/r3.anchor: عن شعيب الجبائي قال : اسم الرسولين الذين قالا : اذ ارسلنا اليهم اثنين شمعون ويوحنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r6.speaker: قتادة وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r6.claim: Qatada and others say the messengers were disciples sent by Jesus after he was raised and the one made to look like him was crucified; the disciples then dispersed, and this story concerns those who went to Antioch.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r6.anchor: فقال قتادة وغيره: كانوا من الحواريين الذين بعثهم عيسى عليه السلام حين رفع وصلب الذي ألقي عليه شبهه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r7.claim: Another group says the messengers were prophets sent by God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r7.anchor: وقالت فرقة: هؤلاء أنبياء من قبل الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r8.claim: The author favors the view that they were prophets because the townspeople's reply that they were ordinary humans suits a claim to divine messengership; the other view remains possible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r8.anchor: وهذا يرجحه قول الكفرة ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا فإنها محاورة إنما تقال لمن ادعى الرسالة عن الله تعالى والآخر محتمل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r10.claim: God sent two messengers to call the town to worship Him alone and to guidance and faith; after their rejection He reinforced them with a third, completing the proof. A man came running, believed, and was killed; the people persisted in disbelief and were silenced by a heavenly cry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r10.anchor: واللازم من الآية أن الله تعالى بعث إليها رسولين فدعيا أهل القرية إلى عبادة الله تعالى وحده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r11.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r11.claim: The majority read فعززنا with a doubled z, meaning that God strengthened and reinforced the messengers; Mujahid and others explain it this way.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء «فعززنا» بشد الزاي الأولى على معنى قوينا وشددنا، وبهذا فسر مجاهد وغيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r12.speaker: عاصم في رواية المفضل عن أبي بكر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r12.claim: In al-Mufaddal's transmission from Abu Bakr, Asim reads فعززنا with a light z, meaning that they prevailed over the messengers in the affair.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ عاصم في رواية المفضل عن أبي بكر «فعززنا» بالتخفيف في الزاي على معنى غلبناهم أمرهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r13.claim: Ibn Masud's codex has فعززنا بالثالث, with the definite article.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p448#2/r13.anchor: وفي حرف ابن مسعود «فعززنا بالثالث» بألف ولام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وكعب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ka'b identify the two messengers as Sadiq and Saduq.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r1.anchor: أحدها صادق وصدوق قاله ابن عباس وكعب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r2.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih identifies the two messengers as Yuhanna and Bulus.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r2.anchor: والثاني يوحنا وبولس قاله وهب بن منبه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r3.claim: Muqatil identifies them as Tuman and Bulus.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r4.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r4.claim: These readers pronounce the zay in fa-ʿazzaznā with a shadda; Ibn Qutayba explains it as strengthening, like describing a camel's flesh as firm.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم فعززنا بتشديد الزاي قال ابن قتيبة المعنى قوينا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r5.speaker: أبو بكر والمفضل عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r5.claim: Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal transmit a light-zay reading from Asim; Abu Ali explains it as overcame or prevailed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر والمفضل عن عاصم فعززنا خفيفة قال أبو علي أراد فغلبنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r6.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains the doubled form as strengthened, citing the Arabic expression for a camel's flesh becoming firm.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة المعنى قوينا وشددنا يقال تعزز لحم الناقة إذا صلب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r7.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r7.claim: Muqatil names the third messenger Shim'un and says he was one of the disciples and Jesus' designated successor.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r7.anchor: قال مقاتل واسم هذا الثالث شمعون وكان من الحواريين وهو وصي عيسى عليه السلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r8.speaker: وهب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r8.claim: Wahb says God inspired Shim'un with the first two messengers' situation and commanded him to support them, so he went to find them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r8.anchor: قال وهب وأوحى الله إلى شمعون يخبره خبر الاثنين ويأمره بنصرتهما فانطلق يؤمهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r9.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r9.claim: Al-Farra says the third had been sent before the first two, although the Quran's sequence makes him appear later.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r9.anchor: وذكر الفراء أن هذا الثالث كان قد أرسل قبلهما قال ونراه في التنزيل كأنه بعدهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r10.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi objects to al-Farra: exegetes hold that the third was sent to support the first two, and someone sent before both would be the first, not the third.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r10.anchor: والمفسرون على أنه إنما أرسل لنصرتهما ثم إن الثالث إنما يكون بعد ثان فأما إذا سبق الاثنين فهو أول وإني لأتعجب من قول الفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وكعب ووهب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r11.claim: One view says God sent the messengers, as the apparent wording indicates and reports from Ibn Abbas, Ka'b, and Wahb relate.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r11.anchor: تعالى أرسلهم وهو ظاهر القرآن وهو مروي عن ابن عباس وكعب ووهب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r12.speaker: قتادة وابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r12.claim: Qatada and Ibn Jurayj say Jesus sent them; this can be attributed to God because they were messengers of His messenger.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p10#2/r12.anchor: والثاني أن عيسى أرسلهم وجاز أن يضاف ذلك إلى الله تعالى لأنهم رسل رسوله قاله قتادة وابن جريج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568#2/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568#2/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq, relaying Ibn Abbas, Kaʿb al-Ahbar, and Wahb ibn Munabbih, identifies the town as Antioch, its king as Antikhus son of Antikhus son of Antikhus, and its messengers as Sadiq, Saduq, and Shalum.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق -فيما بلغه عن ابن عباس، وكعب الأحبار، ووهب بن منبه-: إنها مدينة أنطاكية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568#2/r2.speaker: بريدة بن الحصيب، وعكرمة، وقتادة، والزهري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568#2/r2.claim: Burdah ibn al-Husayb, Ikrima, Qatada, and al-Zuhri are also reported to identify the town as Antioch.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568#2/r2.anchor: وهكذا روي عن بريدة بن الحصيب، وعكرمة، وقتادة، والزهري: أنها أنطاكية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that some leading scholars objected to identifying the town as Antioch, promising to explain the problem after completing the story.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568#2/r3.anchor: وقد استشكل بعض الأئمة كونها أنطاكية، بما سنذكره بعد تمام القصة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p568#2/r4.claim: The third messenger strengthened and reinforced the first two.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569/r1.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the messengers told the townspeople that they came from their Creator and commanded them to worship Him alone.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569/r1.anchor: أي: من ربكم الذي خلقكم، نأمركم بعبادته وحده لا شريك له. قاله أبو العالية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569/r2.speaker: قتادة بن دعامة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569/r2.claim: Qatada ibn Diama says the messengers were sent by the Messiah to the people of Antioch.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569/r2.anchor: وزعم قتادة بن دعامة: أنهم كانوا رسل المسيح، عليه السلام، إلى أهل أنطاكية

JISHUMI:v8p5873/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5873/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5873/r1.claim: When messengers arrive successively, each requires a new miracle and renewed law; the passage also permits a shared law for those sent together.
JISHUMI:v8p5873/r1.anchor: واحدة، وأما إذا جاء بعضهم بعد بعض فلا بد من معجز آخر، وشريعة متجددة

JISHUMI:v8p5873/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5873/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5873/r2.claim: The passage supports the permissibility of strengthening a messenger by sending another messenger alongside him.
JISHUMI:v8p5873/r2.anchor: وتدل على جواز تقوية الرسل برسول آخر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r4.claim: Jesus's emissaries were sent to invite the people to the truth; near the city they met Habib the carpenter tending goats, and told him their mission.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r4.anchor: و { المرسلون } رسل عيسى عليه السلام إلى أهلها ، بعثهم دعاة إلى الحق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r5.claim: Habib asked for a sign; the messengers healed the sick, blind, and leprous, including his son, ill for two years; Habib believed, news spread, and many were healed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r5.anchor: وكان له ولد مريض من سنتين فمسحاه ، فقام ، فآمن حبيب وفشا الخبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r6.claim: The king asked whether there was a god besides their idols; they answered that God created him and his idols. He delayed judgment, the people attacked them, or, in another view, imprisoned them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r6.anchor: وقال لهما : ألنا إلاه سوى آلهتنا ؟ قالا : نعم من أوجدك وآلهتك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r7.claim: Jesus then sent Shimon, who entered in disguise, befriended the king's courtiers, and won the king's trust before persuading him to summon the two messengers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r7.anchor: ثم بعث عيسى عليه السلام شمعون ؛ فدخل متنكرا وعاشر حاشية الملك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r8.claim: Asked who sent them, the two said God, creator of everything without partner; the king asked for a concise description, and they said He does as He wills and rules as He chooses.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r8.anchor: قالا : الله الذي خلق كل شيء وليس له شريك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r9.claim: Asked for a sign, they promised whatever the king wished; they prayed for a boy whose eyes were gone, restored his sight, and placed two pellets in the sockets that became seeing eyes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r9.anchor: فدعا بغلام مطموس العينين ، فدعوا الله حتى انشق له بصر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r10.claim: Shimon challenged the king to ask his own god for such a wonder; the king admitted it neither sees nor hears nor harms nor benefits, while Shimon secretly worshipped with the messengers at the idol.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r10.anchor: إن إلاهنا لا يبصر ولا يسمع ولا يضر ولا ينفع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r11.claim: The king said he would believe if their God revived a dead person; a boy dead seven days rose, warned of the seven valleys of Fire, and urged them to believe.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r11.anchor: فدعوا بغلام مات من سبعة أيام فقام وقال : إني أدخلت في سبعة أودية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r12.claim: The boy said heaven's gates opened and a handsome youth interceded for the three; Shimon identified the two messengers, astonishing the king.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r12.anchor: وقال : فتحت أبواب السماء فرأيت شابا حسن الوجه يشفع لهؤلاء الثلاثة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r13.claim: Seeing his words move the king, Shimon advised him; he and some people believed, while Gabriel's cry destroyed those who refused.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r13.anchor: فلما رأى شمعون أن قوله قد أثر فيه نصحه فآمن وآمن معه قوم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r14.claim: فعززنا means strengthened; usage also applies the root to rain compacting earth and to a camel becoming strong in flesh.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r14.anchor: المطر يعزز الأرض إذا لبدها وشدها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r15.claim: A light reading from عَزَّهُ يَعِزُّهُ means that God overcame and defeated the opponents.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r15.anchor: وقرىء : بالتخفيف من عزه يعزه : إذا غلبه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r17.claim: The direct object is omitted to focus on Shimon and the subtle strategy by which truth prevailed and falsehood was humbled.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r17.anchor: لأن الغرض ذكر المعزز به وهو شمعون وما لطف فيه من التدبير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r18.claim: As in saying the ruler judged justly, the parties judged can be omitted because the focus is the manner of judgment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r18.anchor: ونظيره قولك : حكم السلطان اليوم بالحق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r20.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r20.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r20.claim: The first declaration lacks extra emphasis because it begins the report; after rejection, the second adds لَ to answer their denial.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p10/r20.anchor: لأن الأول ابتداء إخبار ، والثاني جواب عن إنكار

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r2.speaker: شعيب
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r2.claim: Shuayb names the two messengers Sham'un and Yuhanna.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r2.anchor: أحدها : أنهما شمعون ويوحنا , قاله شعيب

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وكعب الأحبار ووهب بن منبه
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ka'b, and Wahb name them Sadiq and Saduq.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r3.anchor: الثاني : صادق وصدوق , قاله ابن عباس وكعب الأحبار ووهب بن منبه

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r4.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r4.claim: Al-Naqqash names them Sim'an and Yahya.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj interprets it as increased.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r7.claim: The word can mean made strong, from al-izza, impregnable strength; Arabs say “whoever prevails takes.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r7.anchor: الثالث : قوينا مأخوذ من العزة وهي القوة المنيعة , ومنه قولهم : من عز وبز

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r8.speaker: شعيب
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r8.claim: Shuayb names the third messenger Yunus.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وكعب ووهب
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ka'b, and Wahb name the third messenger Shalum.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r9.anchor: الثاني : شلوم , قاله ابن عباس وكعب ووهب

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r10.claim: The king of Antioch was one of the pharaohs and worshipped idols with the townspeople.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r10.anchor: وكان ملك أنطاكية أحد الفراعنة يعبد الأصنام مع أهلها

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r23.claim: One view is that the men were messengers sent directly by God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r23.anchor: أحدهما : أنهم كانوا رسلا من الله تعالى إليهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r24.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r24.claim: Ibn Jurayj says they were Jesus's disciples; as emissaries of God's messenger, they could be called God's messengers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p10/r24.anchor: أن يكونوا رسلا لله , قاله ابن جريج

MUJAHID:v2p534/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p534/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p534/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses “We strengthened with a third” as “We reinforced them.”
MUJAHID:v2p534/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ فعززنا بثالث ﴾ يعني شددنا

MUQATIL:36:13-15/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:13-15/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:13-15/r2.claim: The two sent emissaries were Tūmān and Yūnus.
MUQATIL:36:13-15/r2.anchor: { إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين } تومان ونونس

MUQATIL:36:13-15/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:13-15/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:13-15/r3.claim: Fa-ʿazzaznā means We strengthened the two apostles with a third, Shamʿūn, who affirmed God's oneness and revived a girl.
MUQATIL:36:13-15/r3.anchor: فقوينا يعنى فشددنا الرسولين بثالث حين صدقهما بتوحيد الله

MUQATIL:36:13-15/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:13-15/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:13-15/r4.claim: Shamʿūn demonstrated his mission by striking the girl's grave with his foot and calling her to rise by God's permission; she emerged and testified that the emissaries were sent.
MUQATIL:36:13-15/r4.anchor: فخرجت الجارية من قبرها، فعرفوها فقالت يا أهل القرية آمنوا بهؤلاء الرسل، وإنى لأشهد

MUQATIL:36:13-15/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:13-15/r5.speaker: الجارية
MUQATIL:36:13-15/r5.claim: The girl warned that accepting the messengers brings forgiveness, rejection brings punishment, and the townspeople would not believe; she asked to return to her grave and did so.
MUQATIL:36:13-15/r5.anchor: فإن سلمتم يغفر لكم ربكم، وإن أبيتمم ينتقم الله منكم، ثم قالت لشمعون: ردنى إلى مكانى

MUQATIL:36:13-15/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:13-15/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:13-15/r6.claim: Only Ḥabīb al-Najjār believed; he was an Israelite who hurried to the messengers, left his work, and had previously been a polytheist.
MUQATIL:36:13-15/r6.anchor: فلم يؤمن منهم غير حبيب النجار، كان من بنى إسرائيل، وذلك أنه حين سمع بالرسل جاء مسرعا فآمن وترك عمله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r1.claim: The opening إذ is in apposition to the earlier إذ in the preceding verse.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r2.claim: Jesus sent two messengers by God's command, named Ṣādiq and Ṣadūq; they met Ḥabīb al-Najjār tending sheep, who asked about their mission and signs.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r2.anchor: أى أرسل عيسى بأمرنا ﴿ اثنين ﴾ صادقا وصدوقا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r3.claim: The messengers said they healed the sick and cured the blind and leper; Ḥabīb's sick son rose after their touch, many others were healed, and the news spread.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r3.anchor: فقالا نحن رسولا عيسى ندعوكم من عبادة الأوثان إلى عبادة الرحمن فقال أمعكما آية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r4.claim: After the king questioned the pair and they were beaten or imprisoned, Jesus sent Simon, who entered in disguise and gained the royal household's trust.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r4.anchor: وقيل حبسا ثم بعث عيسى شمعون فدخل متنكرا وعاشر حاشية الملك حتى استأنسوا به

NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r5.claim: Simon prompted the king to test them; God restored a blind boy's sight and revived one dead seven days, who warned of the Fire and described a heavenly intercessor for the three.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r5.anchor: فدعوا بغلام مات من سبعة أيام فقام وقال إنى أدخلت فى سبعة أودية من النار لما مت عليه من الشرك وأنا أحذركم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r6.claim: The king admitted his idols could neither hear, see, harm, nor benefit; he, Simon, and the messengers believed, while Gabriel's cry destroyed the unbelievers.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r6.anchor: ليس لى عنك سر ان إلهنا لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يضر ولا ينفع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r7.claim: The people of the town rejected the two messengers.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r8.speaker: أبو بكر
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r8.claim: Abū Bakr's reading relates the verb to ʿazza yaʿuzzu, meaning to overcome; God thereby overpowered and subdued the opponents.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r8.anchor: فعززنا أبو بكر من عزه يعزه إذا غلبه أى فغلبنا وقهرنا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r9.claim: The object is omitted to focus on Simon as the means of support and the subtle strategy that made truth prevail and falsehood fall.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r9.anchor: وترك ذكر المفعول به لأن المراد ذكر المعزز به وهو شمعون وما لطف فيه من التدبير حتى عز الحق وذل الباطل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p5/r10.claim: The three messengers together addressed the town's people, saying they had been sent to them.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r8.claim: One view says the two messengers were sent directly by God from the outset.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r8.anchor: قيل: رسل من الله على الابتداء. وقيل: إن عيسى بعثهم إلى أنطاكية للدعاء إلى الله

QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r9.claim: Another view says Jesus sent them to Antioch by God's command; the verse attributes their mission to God because Jesus acted on His order, after Jesus had been raised to heaven.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r9.anchor: وقيل: إن عيسى بعثهم إلى أنطاكية للدعاء إلى الله، وهو قوله تعالى: { إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين }

QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r10.claim: One account says the townspeople beat and imprisoned the two envoys.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r10.anchor: { فكذبوهما } قيل ضربوهما وسجنوهما. { فعززنا بثالث }

QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r11.claim: “Fa-azzazna” means that God strengthened and reinforced the mission with a third envoy.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r11.anchor: أي فقوينا وشددنا الرسالة «بثالث». وقرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم

QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r12.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r12.claim: Abu Bakr from Asim reads the word with a light z; the other readers use the doubled z.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r12.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم: «فعززنا بثالث» بالتخفيف وشدد الباقون

QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r13.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r13.claim: Al-Jawhari says both light and doubled forms mean strengthening; al-Asma'i cites al-Mutalammis's line to attest this usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r13.anchor: قال الجوهري: وقوله تعالى: { فعززنا بثالث } يخفف ويشدد أي قوينا وشددنا

QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r14.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r14.claim: Al-Asma'i cites a line by al-Mutalammis using “ta'azzaza” for meat becoming stronger or firmer, supporting the readings' shared meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r14.anchor: قال الأصمعي: أنشدني فيه أبو عمرو بن العلاء للمتلمس: أجد إذا رحلت تعزز لحمها

QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r15.claim: An alternative distinguishes the forms: the light form means to overcome and subdue, as in “wa-azzani fi al-khitab,” while the doubled form means to strengthen and increase.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r16.claim: In the story, Jesus' two envoys met Habib al-Najjar, the shepherd of a few sheep and the man associated with Surat Ya-Sin; he invited him to God, healed his ill or possessed son by God's permission, and Habib believed. The story identifies him as the man who came from the farthest part of the city.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r16.anchor: فلقيا شيخا يرعى غنيمات له وهو حبيب النجار صاحب «يس» فدعوه إلى الله

QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r17.claim: After the envoys healed many sick people, the king summoned them. They identified themselves as Jesus' messengers, offered healing of the congenitally blind, leprous, and sick by God's permission, and called for worship of God alone; the king moved to strike them.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r17.anchor: فأرسل الملك إليهما وكان يعبد الأصنام يستخبرهما فقالا: نحن رسولا عيسى. فقال: وما آيتكما

QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r18.speaker: وهب
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r18.claim: Wahb says the king jailed and flogged the two envoys one hundred lashes; when Jesus learned of it, he sent a third.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r18.anchor: وقال وهب: حبسهما الملك وجلدهما مائة جلدة فانتهى الخبر إلى عيسى فأرسل ثالثا

QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r19.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r19.claim: One account identifies the third envoy as Shimon al-Safa, chief of the apostles, sent to support the pair; he befriended the king's court, gained the king's confidence, and feigned agreement with the king's religion before asking about the prisoners.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:13-14/r19.anchor: قيل: شمعون الصفا رأس الحواريين لنصرهما فعاشر حاشية الملك حتى تمكن منهم

QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r1.claim: In the story, the envoys healed a blind boy by prayer and clay pupils; the amazed king then asked if they could revive a boy dead for seven days. The envoys prayed openly and Shimon secretly, and the dead boy returned to life, warned the people of the seven fire-filled valleys he had seen, and testified to God, Jesus, and the messengers, naming Shimon the best of them.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r1.anchor: فجيء بغلام ممسوح العينين موضع عينيه كالجبهة، فدعوا ربهما فانشق موضع البصر

QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r2.claim: The revived boy's testimony led Shimon to identify himself as the Messiah's envoy; the king and many people believed, while others disbelieved.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r2.anchor: فأعلمهم شمعون أنه رسول المسيح إليهم، فأثر قوله في الملك، فدعاه إلى الله

QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r3.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r3.claim: Al-Qushayri says the king believed but his people did not, and Gabriel's cry caused all remaining disbelievers to die.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r3.anchor: وحكى القشيري أن الملك آمن ولم يؤمن قومه، وصاح جبريل صيحة مات كل من بقي منهم من الكفار

QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r4.claim: Another report says Jesus' envoys worried that they could not speak the town's language; God put them to sleep, angels carried them to Antioch, and they awoke speaking its people's language. The account links this to God's strengthening Jesus with the Holy Spirit.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r4.anchor: روي أن عيسى لما أمرهم أن يذهبوا إلى تلك القرية قالوا: يا نبي الله إنا لا نعرف أن نتكلم

QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r5.claim: The townspeople objected that the envoys were ordinary humans who ate and walked in markets, denied that God sent or commanded anything, and called them liars.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r5.anchor: قالوا مآ أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا } تأكلون الطعام وتمشون في الأسواق

QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r6.claim: The envoys swear that God knows they were sent and say their only duty is to convey clearly that God is one.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r6.anchor: فقالت الرسل: { ربنا يعلم إنآ إليكم لمرسلون } وإن كذبتمونا { وما علينآ إلا البلاغ المبين }

DURR-FULL:v7p48/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r10.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r10.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the town was reportedly a Roman settlement to which Jesus sent two men, whom its people rejected.
DURR-FULL:v7p48/r10.anchor: عن ابن جريج رضي الله عنه في قوله {أصحاب القرية إذ جاءها المرسلون} قال: ذكر لنا أنها قرية من قرى الروم
